data.body: RP-01 D2 clarification: a truncated failed response on retry has correctness risk beyond extra recomputation. The discarded tail can contain valid material findings even when the overall JSON fails parsing/validation. A retry can then emit a schema-valid replacement containing only findings visible in the prefix; Pydantic validates shape, not completeness, so the omission may be silent. Concrete Rebar case: CompletionVerdict findings and legacy criteria both default to empty, and PASS with no findings is valid. Reconciliation can recover named failures from a populated criteria manifest but cannot recover findings omitted from both. Truncation can also remove the location relevant to the validation error and presents a counterfactual assistant turn. This reduces to work-only only if all material information is independently present in authoritative input and the model fully recomputes rather than edits the partial draft; Rebar cannot prove that generically. Common formatting-only failures are already repaired deterministically before retry, making the remaining failures a poor population for assuming the tail is irrelevant. Safe policy space is all-or-nothing: send the complete failed response when the complete operation fits, or fail closed / explicitly regenerate from complete authoritative inputs without presenting a partial response as history. Prefix truncation is not cost-only. Research note updated; D2 remains pending.
